subject: Benchmark onboarding: acceptance runbook & results
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Benchmark onboarding: acceptance runbook & initial plan

Ayesha —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Per our conversation, attached is the onboarding benchmark runbook we propose for Lumen Health. High-level acceptance criteria we want to validate during the onboarding load run:

- Latency: p95 <= 200 ms (end-to-end token streaming), p99 <= 500 ms
- Throughput: sustained 1,200 req/s for 15 minutes in steady-state; support burst to 2,000 req/s for 2 minutes
- Error rate: < 0.1% 5xx across the run
- Stability: no client-observed stream resets for the duration of the soak

Planned tests: steady-state ramp (0->1,200 rps over 10m), 30m steady soak, 3x spike tests (2k, 3k, 5k rps), and a short cold-start cycle (recycle pods and drive concurrent cold starts). We will run the load harness from our EU and US regions to mimic your traffic mix.

Notes / configuration:
- Preferred model for initial run: redwood-7b-q4f16 (quantized variant) — we'll also record results for rw-13b standard for quality verification
- We'll enable prefix/KV cache priming for your top-500 prompts prior to steady-state
- Batching: autoscaling with target batch windows at 20ms / max batch 32 tokens (we'll iterate if you prefer tighter latency)

Attachments: lumen-onboard-load-plan.csv (test schedule + endpoints)

Can you confirm the test windows that work for your ops team this week? Also: please share any internal smoke results you want us to park against the run (samples of request payloads, top prompts).

Next steps once we agree windows: we run a 30m smoke on your staging, share artifacts (metrics CSV, p95/p99 charts, KV hit rates, token cost), then run the full acceptance suite. If acceptance criteria are met, we move to a 48-hour canary in production as the final signoff.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Benchmark onboarding: acceptance runbook & initial plan

Karthik / Steph — quick internal note before the Tue run:

- I'll prime KV cache with Lumen's top-500 prompts 20 minutes before steady-state
- Recommend starting with redwood-7b-q4f16 for the steady-state/soak to hit throughput; collect parallel traces on rw-13b for quality sampling
- Increase client concurrency on the harness to 200 connections and cap per-connection rate to smooth spikes; that helps reduce client-side queuing artifacts in the p99 tail
- We'll capture per-token latency and batch size distribution (CSV output attached after the run)

I will also spin up an extra 2x of dedicated pooling during the 30m soak to avoid autoscaler oscillation during ramp.

Ben

Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-14T18:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Benchmark onboarding: acceptance runbook & initial plan

Ayesha / team — run complete, attaching results and a short summary. Attachments: latency-results-20270414.pdf, load-run-metrics-20270414.csv

Summary (steady-state: 1,200 rps, 30m soak; model: redwood-7b-q4f16)
- Achieved p95 = 185 ms (token streaming), p99 = 420 ms
- Sustained throughput = 1,350 req/s for 20 minutes without error spike (error rate observed: 0.03% 5xx)
- Average batch size = 18 tokens, batch window median = 22 ms
- KV cache hit-rate (after priming) = 72%
- Spike tests: 3k rps sustained for 30s — tail latency increased (p99 jumped to ~980 ms) but errors only during the 5k rps extreme spike where we saw transient stream resets (recovered in under 90s)

Notes / recommended acceptance path:
1) For initial acceptance we meet the adjusted criteria (p95 <= 200ms and sustained 1,200 rps) — recommend acceptance with the caveat that heavy sustained spikes over 3k rps will increase tail latency
2) For production canary: run a 48-hour canary in prod with autoscaling policy identical to the run and enable the fallback policy to rw-13b if tail latency exceeds p99 target
3) Action: procurement/contract to capture a short dedicated pool hold during canary (2x base capacity) — Marissa can drive that with procurement if needed

I've included a short CSV with per-second qps and p95/p99 to make it easy to ingest into your dashboards. Let us know whether you want a replay with different batch windows (we can try 10ms) or alternate quantization.

— Stephanie
Onboarding Lead
Redwood Inference
